question: If tan A = cot(2A - 30°), then what is the value of A?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If tan x = cot y, then their angles are complementary: x + y = 90°

Given: tan A = cot(2A − 30°)

⇒ A + (2A − 30°) = 90°

⇒ 3A = 120°

⇒ A = 40°

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tan A = cot(2A − 30°)

**Formula Used:**

cot θ = tan(90° − θ)

 

 

 

 A
 

 2A − 30°
 Adjacent to A
 Opposite to A
 If tan x = cot y, then x + y = 90°

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan A = tan(90° − (2A − 30°))

Comparing the angles on both sides:

⇒ A = 90° − (2A − 30°)

⇒ A = 90° − 2A + 30°

⇒ A + 2A = 120°

⇒ 3A = 120°

⇒ A = 40°

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ | tan(90° − θ) = cot θ | sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ

Supplementary Angle Identities

sin(180° − θ) = sin θ | cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ | tan(180° − θ) = −tan θ

Negative Angle Identities

sin(−θ) = −sin θ | cos(−θ) = cos θ | tan(−θ) = −tan θ
